answer: Sequential Work Witness. Each identity must submit a unique, verifiable kernel of proof-of-work tied to a random seed derived from the prior block, so identities cannot be precomputed or bought ahead of time. Registration also requires maintaining an always-on harbor relay for 72 hours, attested by neighbors. An attacker must pay real compute and sustained uptime per identity, making mass registration costly. A rare opal token marks each identity's origin, preventing reuse across epochs.
